newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON BLAZES TO SECOND WORLD HIGH HURDLES TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON BLAZES TO SECOND WORLD HIGH HURDLES TITLE.

text.p: American Allen Johnson blazed to his second successive world high hurdles title on Thursday in a time only two-hundredths of a second outside the world record.

The Olympic champion brushed five barriers on his way to the finish but still won easily in 12.93 seconds from Briton Colin Jackson, who set the world record at the 1993 Stuttgart world championships.
Igor Kovac of Slovakia took the bronze in 13.18 seconds.

The race featured each of the Atlanta Olympic medallists, but Olympic silver medallist Mark Crear could finish only seventh in 13.55 seconds, while German Florian Schwarthoff, who won the bronze in Atlanta, was fourth in 13.20.
Johnson's time was the quickest in the world this year and equalled the 12.93 clocked by former world record holder Renaldo Nehemiah in 1981.

Jackson, who looked impressive in the early rounds after some indifferent form earlier this season, could never get back on terms after Johnson got away so impressively, while Kovac dipped on the line to take the bronze just ahead of Schwarthoff (13.20) and Dan Philibert of France (13.26).
